the adipose vasucalature plays a critical role in the development, function and metabolic homeostasis of adipose tissue.

angiogenesis and vascular function are essential for adipocyte development, differentiation, and function and that the adipose vas-cular system serves as a cellular reservoir for adipose precursor and progenitor cells that control adipocyte functions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adipose vasucular network is not just a simple passive conduit for nutrient and oxygen supply to the adipocytes but a dynamic and active player in the regulation of the adipose tissue mass, function, and metabolism.
adipose tissue is a complex, dynamic organ that is regulated by a myriad of signals from the vascular and immune systems.

adipocyte-derived factors and adipose vascular cells play an important role in regulating adipocyte functions, and adipocyte-derived factors are essential for angiogenic and vascular remodeling in adipose tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adipose tissue vasculature is a dynamic organ that is critical for adipogenesis and adipocyte functions.
angiogenesis in adipose tissue is a key regulator in the development, function and remodeling of adipose tissue.

adipose angiogenesis and vasoculture are important for adipogenesis and adipocyte metabolism, and that targeting the adipose vascular system may offer novel therapeutic approaches to treat obesity and metabolic diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vascular system is a key regulator of adipose function and metabolism.
angiogenic factors are not merely pro-angiogenic, but also modulate the adipose vasulature to regulate adipocyte function and metabolism.
angiogenesis and vasculo- adipose interactions are essential for the maintenance of adipose tissue mass.
